cases.prompt: I want every PR to fail if the site gets slow. Can you set up a Lighthouse performance gate for my Next.js app?
expectations: Adds a single lighthouserc.cjs as the one source of truth for budgets and assertions.
Sets Core Web Vitals budgets at Google good thresholds: LCP <= 2500 ms, TBT (INP lab proxy) <= 200 ms, CLS <= 0.1.
Gates category floors as errors: performance >= 0.9, SEO >= 0.95, accessibility >= 0.95, best-practices >= 0.9.
Adds the lhci npm script (lhci autorun --config=./lighthouserc.cjs) and a GitHub Actions workflow that blocks PRs.

cases.prompt: My Lighthouse check passes locally but keeps flaking red in CI. What's wrong?
expectations: Prescribes aggregationMethod: "median-run" so the gate compares the median across runs.
Requires numberOfRuns >= 3 (odd numbers give a clean median).
Suggests raising numberOfRuns to 5 if runs are still flaky and ensuring nothing else competes for CPU on the runner.
Explains single-run gates flake constantly due to cold caches and CI noise.

cases.prompt: I added an assertion for the interaction-to-next-paint audit as an error and now CI fails even on good builds. Help?
expectations: Says the experimental interaction-to-next-paint audit should be a warn, not an error, because it is not present in every Lighthouse build.
Explains INP is a field metric with no direct lab audit, so the lab gates on TBT at the same 200 ms budget as an error.
Keeps total-blocking-time as the error-level INP proxy.
Notes hard-failing on a missing audit is the cause of the failure.

cases.prompt: I pointed Lighthouse at my localhost dev server so it runs fast in CI. Is that good enough?
expectations: Rejects auditing the dev server; dev-server numbers are meaningless for a budget.
Requires gating the production build: run build then start the production server (startServerCommand / startServerReadyPattern).
For purely static output, allows collect.staticDistDir pointing at the build folder instead of a server.
Notes local pnpm build && pnpm lhci should reproduce exactly what CI does.

cases.prompt: When the Lighthouse check fails in CI I can't see why. How should the workflow be set up?
expectations: Uploads Lighthouse reports with if: always() so a red check is debuggable even on failure.
Triggers the workflow on the app path and the workflow file itself so config changes are self-testing.
Uploads the .lighthouseci report directory as a CI artifact.
Points the reader to open the artifact and read the failed audit's Opportunities/Diagnostics rather than raising the budget.
